title: Add types for quantization profile status + expose execution mode in route settings responses
author: Ibrahim Khan
description: Context: Backend now tags requests with quantization execution metadata and exposes route-level quantization settings via the Console API endpoints (see redwood monorepo PRs: pr_28833_add_quantization_execution_metrics_tags, pr_28861_console_api_endpoint_route_quantization_settings). Customers asked to be able to programmatically verify whether a given route is currently running quantized vs baseline (e.g., for background summarization only, and for debugging JSON-mode regressions). This SDK change adds typed surfaces so apps can (a) read route settings and (b) inspect the quantization execution mode / active profile in responses without relying on untyped `any` or stringly-typed parsing. Changes: 1) Introduce `QuantizationExecutionMode` and `QuantizationProfileRef` types (id + version) and a `QuantizationStatus` shape returned by route config reads. 2) Extend `RouteSettings` / `GetRouteResponse` to include an optional `quantization` block with: `enabled`, `canaryPercent`, `mode` (baseline|quantized|fallback), and `activeProfile` (id/version) when available. 3) Add a narrow, backwards-compatible `X-Redwood-Quantization-Mode` + `X-Redwood-Quantization-Profile` response header extraction helper (opt-in) for customers who want per-request inspection even when they don’t call the route-settings endpoint. 4) Update generated OpenAPI-derived types to keep `quantization` optional and tolerant of older control planes (Private/Dedicated lag). Compatibility: This is non-breaking. All new fields are optional and guarded behind feature detection. Where the server returns unknown enum values, we preserve the raw string in `modeRaw` and map to `mode='unknown'` to avoid runtime throws. Example usage: `const route = await client.routes.get({ routeId }); if (route.settings.quantization?.mode === 'quantized') { ... }` and `const { quantization } = RedwoodResponseIntrospection.fromResponse(res);` Testing: Adds unit tests for header parsing + JSON decoding, and runs typecheck against the example snippets. Notes: The names are aligned with the control-plane docs (‘route-scoped enablement’) and the console UI terminology (‘canary percent’).
commits: sdk: extend RouteSettings/GetRouteResponse with optional quantization block
sdk: add response header introspection helper + tests
chore: regenerate openapi client + tighten unknown-enum handling
docs: update README snippet for route settings inspection
review_conversation: Alex Martinez (review): Can we avoid throwing if `mode` is an unknown string? Private deployments may lag the control plane by weeks. Also prefer `canaryPercent?: number` vs `canary_percentage` to match the rest of the SDK.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Good call. Updated to map unknown strings into `{ mode: 'unknown', modeRaw: string }` and kept `quantization` fully optional. Also normalized `canaryPercent` to camelCase with the generator transform.

Wei Chen (review): Please add a short README snippet showing how to detect quantization on a per-request basis (headers) vs route config. Also clarify that headers are best-effort and may be absent depending on gateway/version.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Added a small section under 'Debugging & Observability' and noted headers can be missing in older gateways / when disabled.
Dylan Brooks (review): The `activeProfile` shape should be `{ id, version }` only; no registry URI. Console expects to link out using id/version and we don’t want to freeze storage layout in the SDK.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated. Removed `uri` and renamed to `QuantizationProfileRef` with id+version only.

Logan Wright (review): Please make sure header keys match the backend exactly. I think it’s `x-redwood-quantization-profile-id` and `x-redwood-quantization-profile-version` rather than a single combined header.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Confirmed with backend PR and updated helper to support both forms: prefers id/version headers when present; falls back to combined header for older deployments. Added tests for both.
Alex Martinez (approval): LGTM after the unknown-enum handling + README snippet. Thanks for keeping it non-breaking.
Wei Chen (approval): Approved. Docs note looks good.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK now exposes optional quantization status for route settings and adds an opt-in helper to inspect quantization execution mode/profile from response headers. No breaking changes; fields are optional and safe against older control planes.
